summary: This paper introduces the TRAIL cell, a transparency-engineered rf-SQUID unit cell using two series Josephson junctions to achieve Kerr-free three-wave mixing, where the quartic nonlinearity vanishes while cubic nonlinearity persists. A Kerr-free operating ridge is identified in the $\left(\beta, \Phi\right)$ parameter space by tuning junction asymmetry $\beta = I_{c2}/I_{c1}$ and magnetic flux bias, enabling selective control over nonlinear coefficients $c_3$ and $c_4$ in the local potential expansion.
motivation: Standard Josephson traveling-wave parametric amplifiers suffer from unwanted Kerr-type four-wave mixing that degrades phase matching and gain. A central challenge is obtaining strong cubic nonlinearity while suppressing the quartic Kerr term, motivating an engineered approach to the nonlinear response at the elementary cell level.
method: Two Josephson junctions in series with asymmetry parameter $\beta$ form an effective transparent element with non-sinusoidal energy-phase relation embedded in a flux-biased inductive loop. Local expansion around equilibrium points yields coefficients $c_2$, $c_3$, $c_4$ that control stiffness, 3WM, and Kerr nonlinearity respectively. The Kerr-free condition $c_4(\beta, \Phi^\star, \beta) = 0$ defines a one-dimensional ridge in parameter space.
result: For representative parameters $I_{c1} = 2\ \mu$A and $L_G = 120$ pH (screening parameter $\beta \approx 0.73$), the Kerr-free ridge extends to critical asymmetry $\beta_{\mathrm{crit}} \approx 0.66$ where passive 50 Ω matching becomes impossible; the cubic-to-stiffness ratio $\mathcal{F} = |c_3|/c_2$ monotonically increases with $\beta$ along the ridge, with higher $\beta$ yielding larger cubic response but lower cutoff frequency.
